conventions.error_propagation: Platform exceptions remapped to sealed LockdownException hierarchy
conventions.window_message_handling: HandleWindowMessage(message, wparam, lparam) triple for full message context
conventions.fullscreen_reversal: Captured original style/rect stored before any modification; rollback on any step failure

findings.title: Clipboard handler called EmptyClipboard — destroys legitimate clipboard content
findings.description: WM_CLIPBOARDUPDATE fires on every clipboard change, not just paste. The handler called EmptyClipboard() immediately, racing with legitimate copy operations and destroying their source data.
findings.evidence: OpenClipboard(hwnd_); EmptyClipboard(); CloseClipboard(); inside WM_CLIPBOARDUPDATE handler
findings.required_action: Remove EmptyClipboard() entirely. Violation detection only — never mutate clipboard from this handler.
findings.resolution: EmptyClipboard() removed. Handler now only emits a violation event; clipboard state is never modified.
references: CODING_STANDARDS_APP.md: do not mutate shared state from event handlers

findings.title: Clipboard violations routed to process EventChannel — Dart cannot receive them
findings.description: SendViolationEvent('process', ...) for clipboard violations meant the clipboard violations were sent to the process_event_sink_ stream. Dart's ClipboardMonitorChannel had no EventChannel receiver.
findings.required_action: Route clipboard violations to 'clipboard' channel. Add clipboard_event_sink_ member and kClipboardEvents registration. Add EventChannel to ClipboardMonitorChannel Dart class.
findings.resolution: Dedicated clipboard_event_sink_ added; kClipboardEvents registered; ClipboardMonitorChannel.dart gains EventChannel for violations stream.

findings.title: Fullscreen violation stream registered but never emits — window_event_sink_ dead code
findings.description: The window EventChannel was registered and window_event_sink_ was declared, but HandleWindowMessage never sent any events to it. The fullscreen violations stream was effectively empty.
findings.evidence: No SendViolationEvent('window', ...) call found in original HandleWindowMessage
findings.resolution: HandleWindowMessage now watches WM_KILLFOCUS and WM_SYSCOMMAND for fullscreen-escape vectors and emits FULLSCREEN_EXIT to window_event_sink_.

findings.title: Keyboard hook forwarded wParam=0 for non-blocked keys instead of the original wParam
findings.description: CallNextHookEx(nullptr, nCode, 0, lParam) passed 0 as wParam for the non-blocking path, corrupting the keyboard event for downstream hooks and the OS. The original wParam must be forwarded unchanged.
findings.required_action: Pass the original wParam: return CallNextHookEx(nullptr, nCode, wParam, lParam);
findings.resolution: Both early-bail and fall-through paths now forward CallNextHookEx(nullptr, nCode, wParam, lParam) with the original wParam.

findings.title: EnforceFullscreen did not rollback on partial failure — left window in half-stripped state
findings.description: If GetMonitorInfo or SetWindowPos failed after SetWindowLong succeeded, the original_style_ was never restored. The window remained with WS_CAPTION stripped even though fullscreen failed.
findings.evidence: SetWindowLong → GetMonitorInfo → SetWindowPos with no rollback between steps
findings.required_action: After every failing step, call SetWindowLong(GWL_STYLE, original_style_) and SetWindowLong(GWL_EXSTYLE, original_ex_style_) to restore before returning the error.
findings.resolution: All three failure paths (SetWindowLong, GetMonitorInfo, SetWindowPos) now rollback to original_style_/original_ex_style_ before returning the error. ExitFullscreen also checks the SetWindowLong return value.

findings.title: Destructor did not restore fullscreen state before destroying the plugin
findings.description: ~LockdownPlugin() only uninstalled the keyboard hook and unregistered clipboard listener. If fullscreen was still enforced, the window remained in a WS_POPUP state after the plugin was destroyed.
findings.evidence: Destructor called UnhookWindowsHookEx + RemoveClipboardFormatListener but not SetWindowLong restore
findings.required_action: Call a dedicated ExitFullscreenForTeardown() at the top of the destructor to restore original_style_/original_ex_style_/original_rect_.
findings.resolution: Destructor now calls ExitFullscreenForTeardown() first; ExitFullscreenForTeardown() is a best-effort version of ExitFullscreen that never propagates errors.

findings.title: shortcuts_blocked_ accessed from keyboard hook thread and method-channel UI thread without synchronization
findings.description: KeyboardHookProc reads shortcuts_blocked_ directly (bool&) from the hook callback thread. Method channel handlers on the UI thread wrote it. No synchronization.
findings.evidence: if (instance_ && instance_->shortcuts_blocked_) — direct bool read from hook thread
findings.required_action: Change shortcuts_blocked_ to std::atomic<bool>. Use .store() when writing from the UI thread and .load() when reading from the hook thread.
findings.resolution: shortcuts_blocked_ and clipboard_blocked_ are now std::atomic<bool>. Constructor uses .store(false) rather than member-init to avoid ambiguous copy-init on atomic.

findings.title: WM_CLIPBOARDUPDATE fires on any clipboard write, not just paste — potential false positives
findings.description: GetClipboardSequenceNumber() was not used to distinguish internal writes (which we expect) from external writes (which are the actual violation). A future review flagged that every external clipboard copy operation would fire a violation.
findings.evidence: Original implementation only checked GetClipboardOwner() != hwnd_ without sequence-number comparison
findings.required_action: Use GetClipboardSequenceNumber() baseline comparison. Arm baseline at BlockExternalPaste time, update on every WM_CLIPBOARDUPDATE, only fire violation when delta AND owner != hwnd_.
findings.resolution: last_clipboard_sequence_ (std::atomic<DWORD>) baseline armed at blockExternalPaste time, updated on every WM_CLIPBOARDUPDATE. Violation fires only when sequence number changed AND owner != app window.

findings.title: SC_CLOSE (Alt+F4) bypassed the keyboard hook detection path
findings.description: WM_SYSCOMMAND with SC_CLOSE is processed at the window-manager level, bypassing the keyboard hook. The keyboard hook already blocked VK_F4+alt, but if that hook failed or was downgraded, SC_CLOSE would still close the window.
findings.required_action: ADVISORY: Add SC_CLOSE to the WM_SYSCOMMAND detection list for defense-in-depth. Primary defense remains the keyboard hook.
findings.resolution: SC_CLOSE added to the WM_SYSCOMMAND detection list alongside SC_RESTORE/SC_MAXIMIZE/SC_MINIMIZE/SC_KEYMENU/SC_TASKLIST.

findings.title: Verification gates (build, test, analyze) could not run — toolchain unavailable
findings.description: Flutter, Dart, CMake, and MSVC are not present in PATH. The native C++ compilation, Dart code generation (build_runner), flutter analyze, and flutter test could not be executed. All findings above are from static review only.
findings.required_action: Gate commands must be run manually in a Windows environment with the full Flutter toolchain installed: flutter pub get && dart run build_runner build && flutter analyze && flutter test && flutter build windows

verdict_reason: All HIGH blocking findings resolved. 4 MEDIUM findings resolved. 2 NOTED findings (clipboard sequence semantics, SC_CLOSE defense-in-depth) addressed. 1 NOTED finding about toolchain unavailability is an environmental constraint, not a code defect. Phase 03 code reviewed by three independent passes; all critical defects are fixed.
